text:
A: Hi! Hello! Can you hear me okay?
B: Yes, yes, perfect. Hello! Abdul. And you're Marta, the lady with the books!
A: Ha, everyone's saying that today. Yes, that's me. How are you doing?
B: Good, thank you, little bit tired. Late shift yesterday. How about you, how is your day?
A: Erm, long. I'm a pharmacist, cardiology wards, so lots of drug charts. And I'm a bit shattered. Where are you based?
B: Leyton. East London.
A: No way! I'm in Walthamstow, just off Hoe Street. And I swim at the Leyton pool, the freezing one.
B: Ah, the leisure centre! I walk past it every day. Neighbours, we are! And hospital also, I'm a porter, Whitechapel. Sixteen years.
A: Oh, I love porters, honestly. You lot keep the whole place running. When a porter doesn't come, nothing moves. The patient's stuck, the bed's stuck, the doctors are stuck.
B: Thank you! Nobody says this! Tell my manager, please.
A: I will, I'll write a letter. Do you enjoy it?
B: Yes, I like it. I like the patients. Old people especially, they're frightened, so I talk, talk. Some of them, nobody comes to visit. Weeks, nobody. Those ones, I remember them, you know. They stay with you.
A: Yeah. Yeah, I know exactly what you mean. I counsel people before discharge, and sometimes there's just no one to explain things to except them, and you worry, will they manage the tablets on their own at home?
B: That's it. You go home, you're still thinking.
A: Totally. Sorry, that got serious quickly! Your photo, I saw the chillies on the balcony. My tomatoes are finally going red.
B: Tomatoes, I have also! Few pots. And the chillies, this year very good. Gurpreet has chillies also, we talked a long time. Chilli club.
A: Can I join with tomatoes, or is it chillies only?
B: You can join, tomatoes allowed. Do you cook?
A: I do most weeknights. Polish things, żurek, gołąbki, and I do a dal, but probably not a very good one.
B: I'm sure it's good. I'm cooking Sunday, fish curry, bhuna. I learned in Brick Lane restaurants long time ago. Shirin does the weekdays.
A: Oh, that sounds amazing. Is there anywhere local you'd recommend? We always end up at the same places.
B: The Turkish grill near Leyton Midland Road. Very good. Mixed grill, big plate, you won't eat dinner the next day.
A: Okay, I'm telling Daniel tonight. He'll be thrilled, he's been marking all weekend. Do you have a sweet tooth? I bake a lot for work.
B: Sweet, oh yes. But Shirin is making me cut the sugar in my tea. Three spoons, now two. Next year one, she says.
A: Two is still very respectable, honestly. As a pharmacist I'm not allowed to say that.
B: Ha! I won't tell anybody. So you're from where, originally?
A: Gdańsk, in Poland. Fifteen years here, though, so I'm sort of half and half now. Bit foreign in both places, if that makes sense.
B: It makes sense. Thirty years for me, since 1993. I go to Sylhet, they say, ah, the London man. I come back here, they say—
